Jeff Commented: I've been struggling with this type of component too - I think in general, our CFR component needs to be re-thought in general. In this instance, I think I agree with Emily's comment about the cluttered look of it. I'm wondering if there's a better way to showcase this. Can we highlight/spotlight in a more integrative way? Does this feature warrant a different modal? Combo of two (i.e. highlight + card explaining new feature). Maybe something similar to how we introduced wallpapers?

Nicole Commented: the sticky bar in the menu is a nice idea, which gives its content quick access and prominence, I wonder if the account is the most important thing to have there
* I could  see that users associate the icons to the right with the account, so help/settings for account and then the x to close the menu
* What else would make sense in a sticky part of the menu? What are highly used items that users want quick access to?

Nicole Commented: while submenus clean up the IA, I wonder if this adds a barrier to finding what users are actually looking for since the interaction of navigating in and out of submenus vs. scrolling down a longish list feels heavier, also a lot of the site actions like bookmark, request desktop site and so on seem to be frequently used items per survey + telemetry
Nicole commented: the repeating arrow icon for bookmarks, history, downloads feel monotonous and I wonder if users get the idea behind it or if it would be more beneficial to use established icons
Nicole Commented: do we need the home icon since it does roughly the same as the plus, at least for now, or could we merge them? what do users do on home, how successful is home?

Nicole Commented: the page controls menu is interesting, I wonder if a simple list would be an alternative to avoid horizontal scrolling and show all the options in one view;  do you envision a way to automatically/manually 'promote' frequently used items to the surface level so that users don't have to navigate into the menu?

Nicole Commented: the address bar feels heavy with all the icons and options, do you see opportunities to slim it down? what is the most to least relevant item, what is needed and what not, e.g. could we hide the forward arrow until users navigate back from a site?
On desktop, we are only displaying a language code for pages that have already been translated. Otherwise, it is just the icon. We could choose to use just the icon here or add "Translate" as text.

@Aarjav Pandya "Page controls" is just an initial name idea and would need to be validated if we are keeping this menu. I shortened the text a bit here as well but would want to revisit as this feature is finalized.
What does customize mean? Why does it come before cookies? (Also What is cookies?)
I prefer our current CFR design to this because it takes up less real estate (Having X instead of dismiss saves a lot of room). The sparkles & text in the corner make it feel cluttered IMO.
Let me work on copy here & for the empty state

I agree that the dividing line here is confusing and a little arbitrary. If we remove night mode and have only 5 items (and usually 4 because Open in App is conditional only on Android), do we even need it?
I still feel this should be at the bottom of this list because it is conditional.
I think we should move Night Mode into Settings. It was added before iOS made this setting easier to change on a global level and it gets very low clicks as is.

I have reservations about including What's New as a menu item. I think that Settings and Help are more appropriate places for this content. It's one of the least clicked items on the homepage menu, and I don't think adding it to the website menu will change that. It adds clutter and I think there are other opportunities to talk about updates elsewhere in the product.
